BLOCKER: CL-006 violated: `gate1_5` records status "dispositioned below" but the design embeds no Gate 1.5 findings or dispositions; approval is invalid while any BLOCKER/MAJOR is PENDING.

Migration/grandfathering rule is non-deterministic: "created before enforcement" has no pinned cutoff (commit SHA or UTC timestamp). Without it, any legacy MATERIAL_CHANGE approval can be claimed as grandfathered, voiding the ordering invariant.
MAJOR: AC-1 predicate undefined: "cannot carry arbitrary executable content" has no specified allowlist/deny mechanism (script tags, fenced code, include directives, links to executable paths). Without a content-class spec, the validation is implementer-interpreted and drift-prone.

Duplicate validation risk: derived-doc/excluded-content checks are spread across `review_budget.py`, `architect_review_check.py`, and `excluded_content_check.py` with no named shared owner; plan a single generator-authority helper to avoid divergent checks (guardrail 10).

Ancestry "no review-relevant changes" is asserted but the review-relevant path set is not pinned to the same source as the review budget/excluded-content config; divergence would silently weaken coverage.
Failure matrix omits two AC-required negatives (missing `at` timestamp, stale/older review evidence); only older approval and non-ancestor are enumerated — AC-4 incomplete in the pack.
MINOR: Rollback inconsistency: item rollback says "Revert the change"; design_pack adds "regenerate docs; re-run gates" — state the full ordered rollback including doc regeneration.
`out_of_scope: ['Not specified.']` — needs explicit boundaries (e.g., no changes to review lifecycle docs, no Gate 2 tooling) to constrain review scope.

No test asserted for stability of the observability contract (`DERIVED_DOC_STALE`, `MATERIAL_APPROVAL_ORDER`, `REVIEW_HEAD_NOT_ANCESTOR`, `DESIGN_PACK_CONFIG`); error codes are a public contract and should be pinned by tests.
Security invariant weak: "no tenant data" is stated but derived docs are rendered into browsable output; state sanitization/escaping expectations for injected markup even in tooling docs.
NIT: "One 2.5 on the hardening candidate" in requirements is a process note, not a requirement — move to acceptance_evidence.
Performance note "bounded" lacks a concrete bound (e.g., no network, O(files) with cap) for the docs generator check.
SUMMARY: Design direction is sound (tooling-only, reversible, observability via failure codes) and satisfies the language rule (Python tooling/tests). Approval is blocked by the missing Gate-1.5 findings/dispositions embedding (CL-006) and a non-deterministic grandfathering cutoff that undermines the AC-2 invariant. Top risks: unenforceable back-compat rule, undefined executable-content predicate, and an incomplete negative-test matrix.
